analysis: Examined base SSDPrefixCache.swift lines 1837-2191 (TTL sweep, startup scan, removal helpers, settleDurableDonation) and head lines 1-656 (config, lifecycle, lookup, endAdoption). The only change (patch @@ -1791,12 +1791,13, head 1794-1800) rewrites retireIndexedEntries to call SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices, taking removalLock per slice and rechecking hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot per slice instead of once for the whole batch. Security-relevant effect under T-041(b): TTL sweep (base 1848-1855) and eviction still retire entries only while the root is safe and owned; per-slice rechecks are at least as strict, and they let other removals interleave between slices. Expiration is computed once (base 1850), so a slice processed later may unlink an entry that was refreshed by a hit in between. That would be a cache miss and recompute, not a disclosure. The epoch is not rotated by per-file removal (detection_hint), so this change does not alter that. The removeInSlices implementation and how it aggregates the result when a slice returns nil are not visible here. If ownership is lost mid-batch, the helper must merge partial results (removed, externalChange) without crashing or overcounting ttlExpired. It also must not skip reconcileExternalRemovals. Integration should verify SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices (likely in another file) for correct result merging, slice bounds and handling of nil slices. No regression to HMAC naming, AAD, TTL bound, salt scoping or staging reservation release (endAdoption head 616-652, close 430-462) was identified.
